claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr contains approximately 20 at.% each of W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr.
The initial WTaTiVZr material has a fine, homogeneous polycrystalline microstructure.
Commercially used pure tungsten has a coarse-grained microstructure.
WTaTiVZr has enhanced plastic strain and toughness relative to pure tungsten.
High configurational entropy stabilizes a refined, homogeneous microstructure in WTaTiVZr.
The refined, homogeneous microstructure delays premature dynamic recrystallization under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
The refined, homogeneous microstructure reduces dislocation pile-up.
The refined, homogeneous microstructure reduces grain-boundary embrittlement and delays grain-boundary fracture.
Reduced dislocation pile-up and grain-boundary degradation permit more uniform activation of slip systems.
Multiple refractory elements produce significant solid-solution strengthening in equimolar WTaTiVZr.
Reduced dislocation pile-up and delayed grain-boundary fracture improve plastic strain and toughness relative to pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature tests, WTaTiVZr will show statistically significantly greater plastic strain than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature tests, WTaTiVZr will show statistically significantly greater fracture toughness than pure tungsten.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply at approximately 1000–1200 degrees Celsius.
The proposed mechanism may not apply at cryogenic temperatures or under extreme loading conditions outside typical service.
Prolonged high-temperature exposure may evolve the WTaTiVZr microstructure in ways not captured by short-term tests.
